.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Aviation section updated for 06z TAFs.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) A storm system impacts the area Thanksgiving into Friday 
with rain and strong to damaging winds.

2) Widespread moderate coastal flooding likely for the 
Thanksgiving AM and PM high tides, with minor to moderate 
impacts for the Friday AM high tide. In addition, widespread 
beach flooding and dune erosion expected along the open water 
shorelines during the times of high tide, with localized 
overwashes possible.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
The Thanksgiving storm remains on track, with the bulk of the 
rain and wind impacts most likely in the afternoon and evening. 

The models are generally in good agreement with the system.
Time/height cross sections indicate the winds in lowest gate blw
1000ft in the RRFS are 5-10 kt lower than the GFS. However, 
the wind gust output from the RRFS is actually higher than these
same llvl winds. For the fcst, mixed down 80% of the GFS h95 
winds and blended in the NBM. This ends up a little higher than 
the NBM90 in most spots. Overall, little change to the actual 
numbers, but did expand the advy nwd thru the rest of the CWA
with over 70 kt at h85 supporting gust potential. The sustained
24kt in the MAVMGJ is also impressive for that site well inland.
The 18Z HRRR suggests that strongest winds could be delayed 2-3
hours, so timing will have to be re-evaluated with 00Z guidance. 

Rainfall amounts remain similar to the previous fcst, with
subtropical moisture transport into the region strongest in 
the aftn and eve. Deep omega and pwats around 1.5 inches will 
allow for heavy rainfall rates at times. An isold tstm is also 
possible due to the lift over 40 kft. rainfall of 1.5 to 2
inches expected in general, with local amounts to 3 inches 
possible. This was supported by the REFS, GFS, and NBM data.

A dry slot ends the rain from SW to NE overnight, with some
light rain or drizzle possibly lingering. The strong upr low and
steep lapse rates should trigger showers on Fri. It will be 
breezy as well on Fri with SW flow. 

.KEY MESSAGE 2...
With a recent full moon, astronomical tides remain rather high and 
many locations need less than a foot to reach minor coastal flood 
benchmarks with the AM high tides, but closer to 2 ft with the PM 
high tides.

A period of gale to storm force ENE winds will affect the region 
Thursday morning into Thursday Night. The region remains between an 
approaching low pressure and strong high pressure to the north. This 
will bring the likelihood for widespread moderate coastal flooding 
with the Thursday AM and PM high tides, with potential for major 
coastal flooding along the western Great South Bay. Other areas
of notes for significant impacts will be the Peconic Bay area 
with funneling of surge towards the Peconic River, and along W 
LI Sound shoreline with moderate water levels combined with high
wave action. Surge up the tidally affected rivers (Hackensack, 
Hudson, and Passaic) will result in minor to moderate flooding 
as well.

The Thursday AM high tide is the higher high tide by at least 1 ft, 
but the peak surge will likely occur Thursday afternoon into 
evening, based on a multi-model mean of peak winds occurring Thu 
aft/eve. This may result in similar water levels for both tidal 
cycles for much of the area. The forecast has been leaned to a blend 
of 75th percentile of Stevens SFAS and NAEFS P-ETSS (good 
middle ground btwn ECMWF and GEFS PETSS) with deterministic 
ETSS/STOFS. The lean towards the higher end water level scenario
to provide a bit of safety margin, if the timing of strongest 
winds is quicker than currently forecast and with expectation of
winds increasing thru the time of high tide Thu AM.

For the Friday AM high tides, winds switch to the southwest. 
Potential for another round of moderate coastal flooding for the 
southern bays of LI and Queens, particularly for the eastern Great 
South Bay. Elsewhere, offshore flow should allow for water to drain 
out of more open water location (LIS and NY/NJ Harbor) resulting
in mainly minor coastal flood impacts. 

For the oceanfront, breaking waves of 8 to 12 ft will result in 
widespread beach flooding and dune erosion during times of high 
tide. There is potential for localized overwashes, exacerbating 
flooding of roadways and vulnerable structures behind protective 
dunes. Along Western LI Sound and Twin Forks, breaking waves of 3 to 
6 ft will result in areas of dune erosion and localized overwashes. 
Wave splashover will exacerbate flooding of roadways and vulnerable 
structures behind protective dunes and seawalls. There is potential 
for isolated damage to shoreline and marina structures as well.

Heavy rain coinciding with the Thursday evening high tides could 
exacerbate street flooding issues along the coast.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
**HIGH IMPACT STORM TODAY AND TONIGHT**

A large storm approaching from the south will will track across the 
Mid Atlantic states today passing to the W late tonight. An 
associated warm front will approach this evening. 

MVFR cigs developing at the NYC metros and along the coast should 
advance slowly northward overnight into this morning. IFR cond, with 
rain becoming moderate to heavy at times, will follow this 
afternoon. 

Winds out of the NE-ENE will ramp up tonight especially after 
midnight. increasing to 20-25kt G30-35kt during the morning push. 
Winds will further increase into the afternoon to 25-35 kt with G40-
50kt, strongest at the NYC metro and coastal terminals. Peak wind 
gusts could be a few kt higher. This will also be accompanied by 
easterly LLWS at 50-70kt at 1500-2000 ft AGL. 

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Timing of strongest winds could be delayed by 1-3 hours. 

.OUTLOOK FOR 06Z Friday through Sunday... 

Late tonight: E winds diminishing to 20-30 kt G35-40kt, then 
becoming SE-S with warm fropa. Rain also diminishes in 
intensity and coverage with warm fropa. 

Friday: Chance of showers with MVFR cond, becoming VFR at night. 
SW winds G25-30kt, becoming W after midnight. 

Saturday: VFR. W winds G20-25kt, diminishing at night. 

Sunday: VFR.

Sunday night: Showers likely with MVFR cond after midnight. 

Monday: Chance of morning showers with MVFR cond. SW winds G20-25kt, 
becoming W in the afternoon and NW at night.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
No changes to the Gale and Storm Warnings. Seas on the ocean 
are modeled to build to over 20 ft at the height of the storm 
in the late aftn and eve, with waves on the Sound and the NY 
Harbor entrance up to around 10 ft. 

Conditions improve a little on Fri, but a SW gale is likely on 
the ocean and maybe on some of the non-ocean waters as well.  
Winds diminish to SCA lvls on Sat, and likely blw SCA lvls on 
Sun. A frontal sys on Mon could produce SCA conditions,
especially on the ocean.
